purpose: Grader-only outcomes. No model execution or host-selection pass is asserted by the presence of these expectations.

artifact-promotion: Bind checks to integrated-18 and the exact artifact, not the earlier PR.
Promote digest-A or verify a necessary target-specific build separately; resolve mutable references before approval/consumption.
Require consumer verification of provenance against trusted origin and candidate, not just generation.
Preserve existing manual release policy and read-only scope.
monorepo-selection: Cover changes since revision-40, including cancelled revision-41.
Include shared dependents, lockfile and build inputs; fall back to broad coverage if discovery is uncertain.
Identify worker's missing check and independently define required workspace/shard coverage.

partial-deployment: Reconcile deploy A's remote state before retrying or cancelling; serialize all competing effects on the target and reject obsolete candidates.
Address old/new schema compatibility and external notifications; code rollback cannot restore either automatically.
Treat missing telemetry as inconclusive and specify a bounded observation/escalation path.

package-release: Choose checks and packaging from the supported OS/consumer contract.
Install and smoke-test actual distributions; preserve signing/publication requirements where established.
Keep manual release eligibility and distinguish upload/publication from consumer installation.
Avoid mandatory service staging, canary traffic, runtime flags or recall guarantees.
pipeline-trust: Prevent untrusted code, cache writers and build hooks from crossing into release authority without a verified trust boundary.
Bind artifact selection and approvals to the exact candidate; a job name or latest label is insufficient.
Keep skipped required tests unverified and prevent promotion.
Keep the review provider-independent and read-only.
measured-efficiency: Reject a speedup claim based on reduced test coverage and one unmatched sample.
Separate queue, setup, execution, critical-path latency and aggregate runner cost.
Recognize extra shard setup and the slower cache restore; preserve database isolation.
Give measurements and a hypothesis without claiming measured improvement or purchasing runners.
provider-handoff: Discover commands and define the stage, artifact, trust, target and acceptance contract.
Use github-actions for actual workflow/event/permission mechanics and verify for relevant execution evidence.
Use verification-authoring only for missing repeatable recipes.
Honor local-write authorization and leave actual remote settings/deployment explicitly unverified.
missing-platform-specialist: Keep the pipeline contract general and use current primary Buildkite documentation for mechanics.
Continue authorized local implementation without inventing a specialist-installation blocker.
Keep remote settings, publication and real deployment outside the request; identify unobserved behavior.
